title: Mastery Challenge: Relations, Bijective Functions & Logic

questions.promptText: Which of the following describes the Contrapositive of the proposition $p \to q$?
questions.explanation: The contrapositive negates and swaps the order of hypothesis and conclusion: $\neg q \to \neg p$. It is logically equivalent to $p \to q$.

questions.promptText: Under what condition is the conditional statement $p \to q$ logically FALSE?
questions.choiceA: When $p$ is True and $q$ is False
questions.choiceB: When $p$ is False and $q$ is True
questions.explanation: The implication $p \to q$ is false if and only if a true antecedent leads to a false consequent ($T \to F$).

questions.promptText: If $f(x) = 3x - 5$ and $g(x) = x^2 + 2$, find the composite value $(f \circ g)(2)$.
What three properties define a Partial Order Relation (POSET)?
questions.explanation: A partial order relation (POSET) is reflexive, antisymmetric, and transitive (e.g., standard inequality $\le$ or subset inclusion $\subseteq$).

questions.promptText: Find the inverse function $f^{-1}(x)$ for $f(x) = \frac{2x + 1}{x - 3}$ ($x \neq 3$).
questions.explanation: Set $y = \frac{2x + 1}{x - 3} \implies y(x - 3) = 2x + 1 \implies xy - 3y = 2x + 1 \implies x(y - 2) = 3y + 1 \implies x = \frac{3y + 1}{y - 2}$. Thus $f^{-1}(x) = \frac{3x + 1}{x - 2}$.

questions.promptText: What is the truth value of the compound proposition $(T \vee F) \wedge (F \to T)$?
questions.explanation: $T \vee F = T$, and $F \to T = T$ (vacuous truth). Then $T \wedge T = T$.

questions.promptText: Which property is satisfied if for all $a, b$, $(a, b) \in R$ and $(b, a) \in R$ implies $a = b$?
questions.explanation: Antisymmetry states that two distinct elements cannot be mutually related to each other in both directions.

questions.promptText: If proposition $p$ is True and proposition $q$ is True, what is the value of $p \oplus q$ (Exclusive-OR)?
questions.explanation: Exclusive-OR ($p \oplus q$) is True if and only if the propositions have opposite truth values. When both are True, $T \oplus T = F$.

questions.promptText: A function $f: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ is defined by $f(x) = x^3$. Which classification applies to $f$?
questions.explanation: $f(x) = x^3$ is strictly increasing (one-to-one) and its range is $(-\infty, \infty)$ (onto), making it bijective and strictly invertible.

questions.promptText: What is the Converse of the statement: "If it rains, then the ground is wet"?
questions.choiceA: "If the ground is wet, then it rains"
questions.choiceB: "If it does not rain, then the ground is not wet"
questions.choiceC: "If the ground is not wet, then it does not rain"
questions.choiceD: "It rains and the ground is not wet"
questions.explanation: The converse of $p \to q$ simply swaps hypothesis and conclusion to $q \to p$: "If the ground is wet, then it rains."
$R$ is reflexive (contains $(1,1), (2,2), (3,3)$), symmetric ($(1,2)$ and $(2,1)$), and transitive. Hence, it is an equivalence relation.

questions.promptText: What is the Inverse of the conditional statement $p \to q$?
questions.explanation: The inverse of $p \to q$ negates both propositions without swapping their order: $\neg p \to \neg q$.

questions.promptText: If $(f \circ g)(x) = 2x + 7$ and $g(x) = x - 3$, find the formula for $f(x)$.
questions.explanation: Let $u = g(x) = x - 3 \implies x = u + 3$. Then $f(u) = 2(u + 3) + 7 = 2u + 6 + 7 = 2u + 13 \implies f(x) = 2x + 13$.

questions.promptText: A compound proposition that is ALWAYS True regardless of the truth values of its constituent variables is called a:
questions.explanation: A statement that is universally true under all truth assignments (such as $p \vee \neg p$) is a tautology.

questions.promptText: What is a compound proposition that is ALWAYS False under all truth assignments called?
questions.explanation: A statement that is universally false under all truth assignments (such as $p \wedge \neg p$) is a contradiction.

questions.promptText: If relation $R$ on set $A$ is defined by $a R b \iff a - b$ is an integer multiple of $5$, what is $R$?
questions.explanation: Modulo congruence is reflexive ($a - a = 0 = 0 \times 5$), symmetric ($a - b = 5k \implies b - a = -5k$), and transitive ($a - c = (a-b)+(b-c) = 5(k+m)$). Hence it is an equivalence relation.

questions.promptText: Under which truth condition is the biconditional statement $p \leftrightarrow q$ TRUE?
questions.choiceA: When $p$ and $q$ have identical truth values (both True or both False)
questions.choiceB: When $p$ is True and $q$ is False
questions.choiceC: Only when both $p$ and $q$ are True
questions.choiceD: When $p$ and $q$ have opposite truth values
questions.explanation: The biconditional ($p \leftrightarrow q$) is true when both propositions agree in truth value ($T \leftrightarrow T$ is $T$, and $F \leftrightarrow F$ is $T$).

questions.promptText: If $f(x) = x^2$ with domain $\mathbb{R}$, why does $f^{-1}$ NOT exist as a function?
questions.choiceA: Because $f$ is not injective (fails the horizontal line test, e.g., $f(2) = f(-2) = 4$)
questions.explanation: An inverse function requires bijectivity. $f(x) = x^2$ on all real numbers is not one-to-one because two different inputs produce the same output.

questions.promptText: What does Trichotomy mean for any two real numbers $a$ and $b$?
questions.choiceA: Exactly one of $a < b$, $a = b$, or $a > b$ must hold
questions.choiceB: $a + b$ must be positive, negative, or zero
questions.choiceD: Both numbers are real, imaginary, or complex
questions.explanation: The Law of Trichotomy states that for any two real numbers, exactly one relation is true: $a < b$, $a = b$, or $a > b$.
